obligation: FSMA intentional adulteration (food defense): Food Processing
basis: Part 121 applies to facilities required to register under FD&C Act section 415 (21 CFR 121.1). All 11 facilities are registered; the 4 packinghouses pack mostly outside growers' produce, so they are not farms, and group counsel's 2024 review applies Part 121 to all 11. Revenue is far above the very small business threshold (121.5(a), 121.3)

obligation: FSMA intentional adulteration (food defense): Crop Farming
basis: Each Crop Farming operation is a farm (21 CFR 1.227) and farms are exempt from registration (1.226(b)); farm activities subject to the Produce Safety standards are also exempt (121.5(d)). Used as a voluntary checklist for fertigation tampering

obligation: FSMA intentional adulteration (food defense): Farm Supply and group
basis: Neither manufactures, processes, packs or holds food at a registered facility

obligation: FDA Produce Safety Rule, records: Crop Farming
basis: Every farm operation is a covered farm (21 CFR 112.4(a)); average annual produce sales are far above the inflation-adjusted $25,000 threshold. Records are kept in the FMIS

obligation: FDA preventive controls for human food: Food Processing
basis: Registered facilities with food safety plans at all 11. Not applicable to farms or to Farm Supply

obligation: Records access (21 CFR Part 1 Subpart J): Food Processing
basis: Persons who manufacture, process, pack or hold food must establish and keep records and produce them within 24 hours of an official request (1.361)

obligation: Records access (21 CFR Part 1 Subpart J): Crop Farming and Farm Supply
basis: Farms are excluded from all of Subpart J (1.327(a)); Crop Farming harvest lot data supports Food Processing's records. Farm Supply does not hold food

obligation: Food Traceability Rule: Crop Farming and Food Processing
applies: Yes for listed foods (FDA will not enforce before 2028-07-20); tracked
basis: Covered farms and facilities that handle foods on the Food Traceability List; enforcement deferred (Pub. L. 119-37, as FDA described at 91 FR 31723). Not applicable to Farm Supply

obligation: H-2A earnings records and statements: Crop Farming
basis: About 9,000 H-2A workers in season; field tally and hours offered in the FMIS are part of each worker's earnings record; statements issued from payroll. Not applicable to the other divisions

obligation: EPA Worker Protection Standard, application and hazard information: Crop Farming
basis: Agricultural employer; pesticide application records in the FMIS feed the required display and must be retained 2 years after the restricted-entry interval expires

obligation: OSHA Process Safety Management and EPA Risk Management Program: Food Processing
basis: Anhydrous ammonia inventories of about 48,000 lb and 61,000 lb exceed the 10,000 lb threshold (1910.119 Appendix A; 40 CFR 68.130)

obligation: OSHA Process Safety Management and EPA Risk Management Program: Farm Supply
basis: Farm Supply stores no anhydrous ammonia or ammonium nitrate

obligation: Reportable Food Registry: Food Processing
basis: Applies to registered food facilities; Crop Farming has no registered facility

obligation: FAR basic safeguarding: Food Processing
citation: 48 CFR 52.204-21 (52.240-93 in awards under a FAR Part 40 class deviation)
basis: The contract files for USDA commodity sales include FAR 52.204-21

obligation: Section 889 prohibition, with the Kaspersky prohibition: Food Processing
basis: The same contract files include FAR 52.204-25 and 52.204-23

obligation: FAR clauses (N42-R04, N42-R05): Crop Farming, Farm Supply and group
basis: No federal contracts or subcontracts outside Food Processing

obligation: CMMC Program and DFARS safeguarding (N42-R02, N42-R03, N31-33-R01, N31-33-R02): all divisions
basis: No DoD contracts and no covered defense information in any division

obligation: PCI DSS v4.0.1 (contract): Farm Supply
basis: Card payments at 120 branches and on the e-commerce site; the acquirer requires an annual report on compliance by a qualified security assessor. No other division accepts cards in scope

obligation: FTC Act Section 5: Farm Supply
basis: Statements to growers and cooperatives about the portal (security, data use, AI performance) and e-commerce privacy statements

obligation: FTC Act Section 5: Crop Farming, Food Processing and group
applies: Yes (background; not analyzed requirement by requirement)
basis: For-profit businesses in commerce; no consumer-facing security or AI claims were found outside Farm Supply

obligation: FTC Safeguards Rule: Farm Supply
basis: Grower trade credit is extended for business purposes; 16 CFR 314.2 defines a consumer by personal, family or household purposes (group counsel memo, 2026-08). Credit files remain under state data security law

obligation: California privacy law (CCPA/CPRA): Farm Supply
basis: Farm Supply has no customers or operations in California

obligation: SEC cybersecurity disclosure: group
basis: The holding company is an SEC registrant; divisions contribute incident facts through the group

obligation: State data security and breach notification laws: all divisions (Florida worked example)
basis: The group holds personal information of workers (including H-2A workers), employees, growers in credit files and online customers in 7 states; each state where affected individuals reside applies, with Florida as the worked example

obligation: OFAC ransomware payment advisory: group
basis: Sanctions screening applies to any ransom payment decision by any division

obligation: CIRCIA reporting: all divisions
basis: No final rule; as proposed it would reach food and agriculture entities through the SBA size-standard criterion. Tracked

obligation: ECOA and Regulation B: Farm Supply
basis: Agricultural trade credit is business credit under Regulation B; relevant to the proposed credit scoring model (AI-007)

obligation: FAA rules for drone operations: Crop Farming
applies: Yes (as they apply to the operation)
basis: Crop Farming flies imaging drones and spray drones (agricultural aircraft operations)

obligation: State AI laws (for example Colorado): all divisions
basis: No division does business in Colorado; operations are in 7 southeastern states

obligation: Buyer agreements: Crop Farming
basis: About 60% of crop value goes to outside buyers whose agreements require notice within 24 hours of any event that could affect product safety, lot traceability or committed volumes

obligation: Retail and foodservice customer agreements: Food Processing
basis: Notice within 24 hours of an event that could affect product safety or supply; annual third-party food safety certification audits

obligation: Grower Agronomy Portal terms (2025) and cooperative assurance requests: Farm Supply
basis: 72-hour incident notice to reselling cooperatives; grower data used only to provide the service; cooperatives have asked for a SOC 2 Type 2 report

obligation: FMIS vendor agreement (inbound notice): Crop Farming
basis: The vendor must notify the group within 72 hours of confirming an incident affecting group data
